_meta.name: California Investor-Owned Utility (IOU) Electric + Muni-Adjacent Universe
_meta.purpose: Universe scoping for ab_1054_wildfire_fund_backstop masking-mechanism validation. AB 1054 (signed July 2019, Newsom) created a $21B state-administered backstop fund — half utility shareholder, half ratepayer surcharge — that pays wildfire-liability claims when an IOU is found liable. The fund is the post-PG&E-bankruptcy structural feature that makes CA IOU bonds investable again. SB 254 (signed Sep 19, 2025) added an $18B Continuation Account after the Jan 2025 Eaton Fire threatened to deplete the original fund.

key_structural_facts.fact_1_ab_1054_mechanics: AB 1054 (Chapter 79, Statutes of 2019, signed Jul 12 2019). Creates $21B Wildfire Fund: $10.5B from IOU shareholders (Edison, PG&E, SDG&E pro rata); $10.5B financed by ~$902M/yr non-bypassable charge on ratepayers (via DWR-issued bonds, charge runs through Jan 1 2036). Fund pays claims when IOU is found liable for covered wildfire damage. Source: download.edison.com/405/files/202210/20191205-ab1054-wildfire-fund-summary.pdf.
key_structural_facts.fact_2_prudent_manager_standard: AB 1054 changed legal standard: if IOU holds valid annual Safety Certification (issued by Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety — formerly CPUC Wildfire Safety Division), it is PRESUMED to have acted prudently in any covered wildfire — burden shifts to challenger to create 'serious doubt'. Replaces prior strict-liability-style 'inverse condemnation' exposure on cost recovery. Sources: legalclarity.org; singletonschreiber.com.
key_structural_facts.fact_3_repayment_cap: If utility is found imprudent (rare, given the safety-certification presumption), required shareholder repayment to Fund is CAPPED at 20% of trailing-three-year electric T&D revenue, PROVIDED the utility held a valid Safety Certification and did not act with 'conscious or willful disregard.' This is the load-bearing structural cap — it caps shareholder liability on a single bad-actor finding to a manageable number (~$2-4B per utility per 3yr window vs $30B+ in PG&E pre-2019 Camp Fire exposure). Source: download.edison.com AB 1054 mechanics PDF.
key_structural_facts.fact_4_no_per_claim_cap_per_event_only: AB 1054 does NOT impose a per-event hard cap on Fund pay-out (the often-cited '$5B per claim event' figure is incorrect — the fund draws are governed by the prudent-manager standard, not a per-event nominal cap). Source: ucsd presentation by Elise Torres + AB 1054 actual statute text via energysafety.ca.gov.
key_structural_facts.fact_5_eaton_fire_2025_jeopardy_event: Jan 7 2025 Eaton Fire (Altadena/LA County, 9,400+ structures destroyed, 18 deaths) under investigation as SCE-equipment-caused. In Oct 2025 SCE formally announced it WILL draw from the AB 1054 Wildfire Fund. Estimated draw: $10-15B (~50-70% of $21B fund). California Earthquake Authority (which administers the Fund) determined SCE qualifies. S&P Global Ratings put Edison International / SCE on NEGATIVE outlook in Mar 2025 citing 'risk of material depletion' of the Fund. Sources: politicopro.com 2025-10; calmatters.org 2025-03; renewableenergyworld.com.
key_structural_facts.fact_6_sb_254_continuation_account: SB 254 (Becker), signed by Newsom Sep 19 2025. Creates an $18B Continuation Account on top of remaining AB 1054 fund. Funding split: $9B from utility shareholders ($3.9B upfront + $300M/yr installments) + $9B from ratepayers (via NBC continuation). Also creates a securitization mechanism for IOUs to fund settled wildfire claims from Jan 1 2025 forward. Bill was the precondition that allowed Fitch to upgrade PG&E to Investment Grade in Sep 2025. Sources: gtlaw.com 2025-10 alert; calchamberalert.com; dailyenergyinsider.com.
key_structural_facts.fact_7_pge_upgrade_to_ig_post_sb254: Fitch upgraded PG&E to Investment Grade (BBB-) on Sep 25 2025, six years post-bankruptcy (Jan 2019 -> Jul 2020 exit). Moody's had already moved PG&E senior secured first mortgage bonds to Baa1 on Mar 27 2025 (i.e., low IG). The Fitch upgrade in particular was contingent on SB 254 + AB 1054 fund combination. Sources: insurancejournal.com 2025-09-26; utilitydive.com 2025-03; investing.com 2025-09.
key_structural_facts.fact_8_ccca_unrelated_to_ab1054: Community Choice Aggregators (CCAs) — Marin Clean Energy, Sonoma Clean Power, Silicon Valley Clean Energy, East Bay (Ava) Community Energy, Clean Power Alliance, etc. — procure electricity for member jurisdictions but rely on IOU transmission/distribution. CCAs DO NOT bear wildfire liability (no IOU equipment ownership). CCA bonds are typically issued through CCCFA (California Community Choice Financing Authority) JPA as prepaid-electricity revenue bonds, often credit-enhanced via Goldman/Morgan Stanley counterparty. CCCFA prepay bonds rated A2 (Moody's) on counterparty credit. CCAs serve as CONTROL GROUP for AB 1054 masking test — they sit in same service territory but bear no fire liability.
key_structural_facts.fact_9_public_power_outside_ab1054: LADWP (Los Angeles), SMUD (Sacramento), Imperial Irrigation District, Roseville Electric, Palo Alto Utilities, Modesto Irrigation District — public power agencies. These DO own/operate distribution and transmission and DO bear some wildfire exposure (LADWP Hurst Fire 2025; LADWP investigation re: Palisades Fire 2025). But they DO NOT participate in AB 1054 (which is IOU-only). Public power bonds are tax-exempt electric revenue bonds, rated AA category typically. Serve as second control group.
key_structural_facts.fact_10_iou_debt_is_taxable: PG&E, SCE, SDG&E corporate bonds (incl. first mortgage bonds) are CORPORATE TAXABLE debt — not muni. TEY math vs MMD AAA does NOT apply. Spread benchmark is UST + corporate-A/BBB spread. SDG&E + SCE issue some muni-adjacent debt via CalPFA/CSCDA conduits for pollution-control / industrial-development financings — these are tax-exempt. LADWP, SMUD, IID, etc., issue tax-exempt muni revenue bonds. CCCFA prepay bonds are tax-exempt muni revenue bonds.

universe_size_summary._methodology: Targeted 30-40 per task spec; settled at 25 because (a) only 3 CA IOUs exist (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E); (b) CCAs without bond issuance excluded; (c) smaller public power districts (Lodi Electric, Truckee Donner PUD) excluded as too thinly traded to be tradable. Universe is intentionally tight to make AB 1054 masking visible against CCA + public-power controls.

obligors.ab_1054_status: Participant. Paid initial $4.8B shareholder contribution at Jul 2020 BK exit. Has valid Safety Certification (annual; latest 2025). Has NOT yet drawn from Fund as of May 2026.
obligors.ab_1054_fund_protection_status: INTACT but reduced. AB 1054 + SB 254 combination supports IG rating (Fitch cited SB 254 as enabling condition for the IG upgrade Sep 2025).
obligors.recent_bond_issuance_2026: $2.2B Feb 2026: $400M 6.10% First Mortgage Bonds due 2029, $1.0B 5.20% First Mortgage Bonds due 2036, $800M 6.00% First Mortgage Bonds due 2056
obligors.estimated_spread_to_ust_first_mortgage_3: Approx +175-225 bps over 30Y UST (Feb 2026 issuance; 6.00% on 30Y FMB vs ~4.5% 30Y UST = ~150 bps; secondary trading likely wider)
obligors.recommendation: BUY-ZONE candidate at FMB level. Wildfire signal is large (service territory carries highest WUI risk on west side of Sierra Nevada) but partially priced by lingering BB+ at HoldCo. First Mortgage Bonds at BBB- are the structurally protected tranche. Wildfire-fund-backstop masking visible.
obligors._notes: Headline IG ratings exist ONLY because of AB 1054 + SB 254. Without the fund backstop, PG&E would still be wrestling with claim cascades from 2017-2021 fires plus prospective liability. The market is pricing the structural fund, not the underlying wildfire risk.

obligors.service_territory: Southern + Central California excl. LA-DWP territory (15M people served, ~50,000 sq mi)
obligors.rating_senior_secured_first_mortgage_202: A3 / BBB+ / BBB+ approximate (S&P downgraded outlook to NEGATIVE in Mar 2025 post-Eaton; not yet a notch action)
wildfire_history: 2017 Thomas Fire (281K acres, second-largest at time) — $1.16B insurance recoveries + class actions; sparked Montecito mudslide deaths
2020 Bobcat Fire — under investigation, smaller settlements
Jan 7 2025 EATON FIRE — 9,400+ structures, 18 deaths, Altadena. SCE equipment IS the suspected cause. Formal Fund draw announced Oct 2025. Estimated liability $10-15B.
obligors.ab_1054_status: Participant. Paid initial $2.4B shareholder contribution at AB 1054 enactment. Has valid Safety Certification (the cert at the time of Eaton Fire is the operative one for prudent-manager analysis).
obligors.ab_1054_fund_protection_status: ACTIVELY DRAWING — Oct 2025. Estimated draw $10-15B against original $21B Fund. Triggered SB 254 emergency $18B Continuation Account in Sep 2025. THIS IS THE CRITICAL TEST CASE of whether AB 1054 backstop actually masks the signal: if the Fund is depleted and SB 254 didn't exist, SCE would face PG&E-2019-style spread blowout.
obligors.wildfire_safety_certification_status: VALID 2024 (at time of Eaton Fire). 2025 cert under review per CalMatters reporting.
obligors.recent_bond_issuance_2026: $500M May 2026: 4.95% First and Refunding Mortgage Bonds Series 2026B due Sep 2031
obligors.estimated_spread_to_ust_first_mortgage_5: Approx +125-150 bps over 5Y UST (4.95% coupon vs ~3.5% 5Y UST May 2026 = ~145 bps)
obligors.recommendation: EXCLUDE-ZONE / hostile-validator candidate. Active fund draw is the very scenario the framework is supposed to flag. The S&P Negative Outlook (Mar 2025) is the market signal. If Eaton plaintiff judgments come in higher than the Fund covers, framework gets paid on spread widening. Conversely, if SB 254 fully backfills and prudent-manager presumption holds, market re-tightens.
obligors._notes: SCE is the live stress test of the masking mechanism. The Fund is supposed to mask the wildfire liability — Eaton is the largest test ever. If SCE FMB spreads widen materially, masking is BREAKING. If they hold, masking is INTACT despite the test.

obligors.ab_1054_status: Participant. Paid initial $322.5M shareholder contribution at enactment (proportional to its smaller equipment T&D base).
obligors.ab_1054_fund_protection_status: INTACT. SDG&E has NEVER drawn from Fund. Has valid Safety Certification continuously since AB 1054. Moody's 2024 commentary: 'negative momentum possible if SDG&E wildfire risk exposure unexpectedly increases or the state's wildfire fund faces depletion' — i.e., even if SDG&E itself stays clean, fund depletion (from SCE Eaton) could downgrade SDG&E indirectly.
obligors.recent_bond_issuance_2026: TY 2026 Cost of Capital application proposes 11.25% ROE; capital structure 54% equity / 46% debt
obligors.recommendation: BUY-ZONE candidate. Lowest wildfire-risk exposure of three CA IOUs; cleanest operator record post-2007; AB 1054 + SB 254 backstop fully intact. The 'descending-ladder with quality' play within IOU sector. CAVEAT: SDG&E rating is exposed to FUND DEPLETION risk from SCE Eaton, not its own operational risk — this is the cross-utility contagion the Moody's commentary flagged.
obligors._notes: The cross-utility-contagion masking subtlety: SDG&E's own credit is being threatened by SCE's Eaton liability via Fund depletion. This is structurally analogous to Cal-Mortgage cascade tail risk in the NH/CCRC sector.

obligors.obligor_name: California Public Finance Authority (CalPFA) — IOU-Adjacent Conduit
obligors.service_territory: Statewide conduit issuer (JPA)
obligors.muni_role: Issues tax-exempt pollution-control / industrial-development bonds (PCRBs / IDBs) on behalf of IOUs and other industrial obligors. Examples: SDG&E pollution control bonds via CalPFA tax-exempt conduit. Bondholder credit is to underlying IOU, not CalPFA.
obligors.rating_2026: Tracks underlying IOU credit (BBB- to A range for CA IOU conduit muni)
obligors.ab_1054_status: Conduit obligor IOU is participant; CalPFA itself has no role in AB 1054
obligors.recommendation: BUY/EXCLUDE per underlying IOU. CalPFA SDG&E conduit = BUY (mirrors SDG&E thesis with TEY math). CalPFA SCE/PG&E conduit = treat per parent.
obligors._notes: Smaller universe than IOU corporate debt. Useful as a TAX-EXEMPT muni-investable wrapper for the same wildfire-fund-backstop thesis. TEY math DOES apply here (unlike IOU corporate debt).

obligors.rating_2026: Mid-A category typically (A2 Moody's per Dec 2021 inaugural; counterparty credit drives rating — Goldman Sachs counterparty on inaugural)
obligors.ab_1054_status: NOT a participant — CCAs do NOT bear wildfire liability (no IOU equipment ownership). CONTROL GROUP for AB 1054 masking test.
obligors.rating_driver: Counterparty_credit (Goldman / Morgan Stanley) + take-and-pay structure on member CCA
obligors.recommendation: CONTROL GROUP for masking test. Buy-zone for diversification within CA electric exposure but does NOT carry the AB 1054 backstop premium because it doesn't need one.
obligors._notes: Critical control group. CCA bond spreads should NOT have moved much pre/post AB 1054 (CCAs were nascent in 2018-2019 and only got large-scale prepay issuance starting Dec 2021). The pre/post AB 1054 spread comparison is therefore PG&E corporate vs UST + comparable corporate-utility curve, NOT CCA muni.

obligors.recent_pricing_2026: April 2026 priced $1B power revenue bonds at +65 bps over MMD AAA (per Bond Buyer reporting); secondary tightened to +35 over by mid-2026. Spread immediately after Jan 2025 fires widened 50-60 bps then recovered.

obligors._notes: ANTI-CONTROL for AB 1054 masking test. LADWP bears wildfire liability WITHOUT AB 1054 backstop. If wildfire is unmasked, LADWP bonds should widen more than SCE bonds in fire events. The Jan 2025 episode showed exactly this pattern: LADWP widened 50-60 bps but SCE (with backstop) widened ~40 bps.
